event.observed: The filter must select in-stock products that are blue or green. With in_stock=false, blue=false and green=true, the generated in_stock AND blue OR green expression returned true.
event.outcome: Grouping the positive color alternatives as in_stock AND (blue OR green) made that record fail the filter. The boolean input values were already correct.

procedures.body:
# Group alternatives under the mandatory boolean condition

## When to apply
When a boolean filter requires mandatory condition A and at least one positive alternative B or C. All boolean values have already been computed correctly.

## Procedure
1. Group the alternatives as (B OR C).
2. Combine the group with the mandatory condition as A AND (B OR C).
3. Verify that A=false produces false regardless of the values of B and C.

## Pitfalls
Do not emit A AND B OR C without grouping. Do not drop the mandatory condition or change the meaning of the already computed input values.

# Convert one-based selection positions to zero-based indices

## When to apply
When a user selects one-based position p in a one-dimensional list of length N, and the interface and target collection use the same element ordering.

## Procedure
1. Validate that 1 <= p <= N; reject an invalid position explicitly.
2. Subtract one exactly once and access index p-1.
3. The first position maps to index 0 and the last position maps to N-1.

## Pitfalls
Do not use a one-based position directly as an index or subtract one twice. This arithmetic assumes the interface and target collection have the same ordering.

event.observed: The filter builder now receives an explicit mode that negates the whole group of color alternatives. The requested rule is in_stock AND NOT (blue OR green), but the emitted in_stock AND NOT blue OR green incorrectly allowed green records.
event.outcome: The builder applied NOT to the complete grouped alternatives in the explicitly negated mode. The existing positive mode retained in_stock AND (blue OR green).

event.observed: The product boolean filter was verified against its truth table and selected exactly the intended products. Joining the selected products with the photos table then duplicated one product with two photos, causing an overstated product count.
event.outcome: Photos were aggregated to one record per product_id before the join. The boolean filter expression was unchanged and the product count became correct.
